requirement_summary: 02_FUNCTIONAL_REQUIREMENTS_AND_PROGRAMS.md NFR-PRIV: '고객별 보존기간과 완전 삭제 증명. 검증: 삭제 요청 후 계약된 보존기간 내 deletion_receipt가 발급되고 retention_state가 DELETED_SIGNED_EXTERNAL_VERIFICATION으로 전이해야 한다.'
subject: SemanticAssuranceV2WorkflowService.retentionDeletionProofCheck via assurance.retention.deletion-proof-check; contracts/retention-deletion-proof-check.v1.schema.json (NEW). Complements the pre-existing ServiceCaseLifecycleService.recordDeletion (real signed-external-verification-receipt-gated deletion, legal-hold blocking, already implemented before this closure) by adding the retention-period timing check the requirement itself names but recordDeletion did not enforce.
coverage_notes: retentionDeletionProofCheckDetectsAReceiptIssuedAfterTheRetentionDeadline is the direct test of the requirement's own named timing rule ('보존기간 내'): a genuinely-present receipt issued after deletion_requested_at + retention_period_days is caught by a real Instant comparison, not merely checked for eventual existence. retentionDeletionProofCheckRejectsADeletedStateClaimedWithoutAReceipt mirrors the discipline ServiceCaseLifecycleService.recordDeletion already enforces in real code (deletion can only be recorded with a genuine signed external verification receipt, never a bare status flip) -- this operation independently re-derives the same rule structurally, rather than trusting a caller's retention_state=DELETED_SIGNED_EXTERNAL_VERIFICATION claim at face value.
open_gap: Operates on a caller-supplied timestamp/receipt-presence representation; it does not itself call ServiceCaseLifecycleService or read a real case's persisted state (same disclosed 'caller-supplied representation, not live system integration' pattern as every real-computation closure this session, though the underlying deletion-receipt mechanism it verifies against IS real, pre-existing, cryptographically-verified code, unlike most other closures this session which have no live counterpart at all). retention_period_days itself is DRAFT/contract-specific per the design doc's own C10 open decision -- this operation accepts it as a caller-supplied input rather than deriving it from any actual customer contract, since no such contract-terms store exists in this codebase.
